The wording defect is real, and I checked it against the code. Line 97 of spec.md says "in every case but one" and then names two exceptions: an unavailable level at 4x4, and a press that needs the confirmation. In `choose()` and the level click handler in play-page.ts (lines 326-341, 361), the unavailable-level press returns early and does nothing. The confirmation press calls `hidePopover()` but sets `returnToSummary` instead of focusing the summary button. So there are two exceptions, and "but one" is wrong. This is a spec-wording nit only. The code matches the intended behaviour, and no user or attacker can hit a runtime problem from it. The finding itself is confirmed. I'd downgrade it to a nit because nothing misbehaves.

contested.title: Toggle listener no longer implements the spec's 'no rules panel open' guard; the spec still requires it
contested.evidence: Spec, «Choosing and closing the sheet» (spec.md:97): 'when `newState` is `closed`, the confirmation dialog is not open and no other popover of the page (the rules panel) is open, move focus to the summary button'. Code (play-page.ts:343-350) checks only that focus is outside the sheet and that the dialog is open. The rules-panel check was dropped ('panelIsOpen removed as dead code', docs/qa/add-level-selector-green-run.txt). The scenario 'A late toggle event does not steal the focus from the rules panel' still passes, but only because focus is on «Зрозуміло», which is outside the sheet. With the rules panel open and focus on the body, the code moves focus to the summary button, which goes against the spec text. red-evidence.md section 3 mutant 10 ('rules-panel guard removed') also describes a guard that no longer exists.
contested.suggestion: Choose one source of truth. Either remove the rules-panel clause from the requirement text, so the outside-focus rule plus the dialog guard is the whole rule, or put back a `rulesPanel.matches(':popover-open')` guard and add a scenario with focus on the body while the rules panel is open. Add a note to mutant 10 in red-evidence.md saying it applied to the earlier listener.
verifierNotes: The finding holds. The toggle listener at src/ui/play-page.ts:343-350 returns early only if focus is on an element outside the sheet (other than the body) or if the dialog is open. There is no `rulesPanel.matches(':popover-open')` check; `rulesPanel` is declared at line 87 but not used in this handler. Spec.md:97 requires the opposite. It says focus moves to the summary button only when no other popover of the page (the rules panel) is open. It also says a late toggle while the rules panel is open must not move focus. The existing scenario at spec.md:140 passes only because focus sits on «Зрозуміло», which is outside the sheet. If the rules panel is open and focus is on the body, the handler calls `summaryButton.focus()`. This can happen after a click on non-focusable text in the panel. That breaks the spec text, though the path is narrow and the severity is minor. I did not check the green-run log or red-evidence.md, so the notes about the dropped guard and mutant 10 are unverified.

The text mismatch is real. Spec.md:97 names a rules-panel guard, and the toggle listener at play-page.ts:343-350 checks only the dialog and focus outside the sheet. But a user cannot reach the case where this matters. The rules panel is `popover="auto"`, and its close button has `autofocus`, so opening it puts focus on «Зрозуміло», which is outside the sheet. The listener returns early in that case. Opening the panel also light-dismisses the sheet. Focus on the body while the panel is open would need an unusual sequence, because clicking elsewhere light-dismisses the panel. I found no user-reachable sequence that steals focus. This is a documentation drift between spec text and code, not a behavior defect. The mechanism is not confirmed as a real-user problem, so I refute it.

rejected.title: Spec still makes 'rules panel not open' a condition of the toggle focus rule, but the code no longer checks it (panelIsOpen removed)
rejected.evidence: Spec line 97 says focus moves to the summary when `newState` is `closed`, "the confirmation dialog is not open and no other popover of the page (the rules panel) is open". The fix round removed `panelIsOpen` as dead code (green-run.txt line 17). The listener now only checks `active !== null && active !== document.body && !sheet.contains(active)` and `dialog.hasAttribute('open')`. The rules-panel case is covered only indirectly, because the panel's `autofocus` puts focus on «Зрозуміло». If the panel is open while focus is on body (for example a click on the panel's non-focusable text before a late toggle), the code moves focus to the summary button, which the spec forbids. The scenario test passes only because its GIVEN puts focus on «Зрозуміло».
rejected.suggestion: Either restore an explicit `rulesPanel.matches(':popover-open')` guard (try/catch, or a state flag kept by the panel's own toggle listener), or reword the spec sentence so the rules-panel clause is the focus-based rule the code implements, and add a scenario with the panel open and focus on body.
verifierNotes:
The code check is as described. The sheet's toggle listener at src/ui/play-page.ts:343 has no explicit rules-panel guard. It returns early when focus is on an element outside the sheet and not on body, and when the dialog is open. The spec's own closing sentence says the rules-panel case is handled by the autofocus of «Зрозуміло» ("so does the autofocus of «Зрозуміло» in the rules panel"), which is the focus-based mechanism the code uses.

The failure scenario is practically unreachable. The rules panel is `popover="auto"`, so opening it closes the sheet. The sheet's closing `toggle` event is queued at that same moment. Focus then moves to «Зрозуміло» through the panel's autofocus. The listener sees focus on a button outside the sheet and returns without moving focus. For the finding's scenario to occur, focus would have to fall to body (for example from a click on the panel's non-focusable text) before a late toggle arrives. Toggle events are dispatched in the same event-loop turn as the state change, so a user click cannot come between them.

What remains is a small wording gap between the spec's parenthetical and the implementation, with no real misbehavior.

Not reproducible. The sheet (src/ui/play-page.ts:75) and the rules panel (line 87) are both `popover="auto"`, so only one can be open at a time. Opening either one closes the other. For the sheet's toggle listener (lines 340-347) to run with the panel open, the sheet would have to close because the panel opened. In that case `showPopover` on the panel runs its autofocus synchronously, and focus lands on «Зрозуміло» (line 101). The sheet's `toggle` event fires afterwards as a queued task. By then `active` is inside the panel and outside the sheet, so the listener returns early and does not move focus to the summary button. The claimed case, with the panel open and focus on body at a late sheet toggle, would need the sheet to close while the panel was open. The sheet cannot be reopened without closing the panel, so that sequence cannot happen. The code's focus-based guard therefore enforces the spec's "no other popover open" condition in practice. At most this is a spec wording mismatch with no observable effect for a user.

rejected.title: Spec says the summary text SHALL be rewritten after a reset, but resetBoard never touches it
rejected.evidence: The Summary button requirement now reads "The visible text SHALL be rewritten after every board that is shown (... also a reset, which shows the same size and level) and after nothing else". `resetBoard()` re-renders cells and clears messages but never calls `syncControls()`, so `summaryLabel.textContent` is never rewritten on reset. The visible value is the same, so users see no difference, but the normative 'rewritten' clause does not match the code and a mutation-observing test would fail.
rejected.suggestion: Either call `syncControls()` (or only the summary line) at the end of `resetBoard`, or change the spec clause to 'reflects' / 'stays equal to' the shown size and level, so reset is plainly a no-change case.
verifierNotes: The finding quotes a spec clause that no longer matches the current spec. Line 5 of openspec/changes/add-level-selector/specs/play-page/spec.md says the visible text is rewritten after the mount, a performed size or level change, and «Нова головоломка». It then says "a reset shows the same size and level and leaves the text as it is, as «Reset button» says". The spec therefore treats reset as a no-change case, which is what the code does: `resetBoard` does not call `syncControls`, and `syncControls` is the only place `summaryLabel.textContent` is set (line 129). No spec clause says the text is rewritten on reset, so there is no mismatch with the code and no mutation-observing test that would fail. The finding's suggested fix (change the clause to "reflects") is already effectively in the spec.

The finding quotes spec wording that is not in the current spec. The current play-page spec (line 5) says the visible text is rewritten after the mount, a performed size or level change, and «Нова головоломка». It then says that "a reset shows the same size and level and leaves the text as it is". So resetBoard not calling syncControls matches the spec. The only call sites of syncControls are line 239 and the mount call at line 366. There is no spec/code mismatch, and the user-visible value is unchanged either way.

rejected.title: In browsers that do not focus buttons on click (Safari), a light dismiss by a click on a cell still moves focus to the summary button
rejected.evidence: The fix keeps focus where it is only when `document.activeElement` is an element outside the sheet other than body. In WebKit on macOS a mouse click does not focus a `<button>`. When a click on a cell light-dismisses the sheet, the focus that was inside the sheet goes to body or to the invoker. The listener then calls `summaryButton.focus()`, which is the light-dismiss focus-steal the fix round targeted; it was confirmed only in Chromium. The spec explicitly allows the 'no element' case, so this follows the spec but can still surprise users.
rejected.suggestion: Record that the fix was verified only in Chromium. Optionally, track the last pointerdown target outside the sheet (a `pointerdown` listener on the root) and skip the summary focus when the close was caused by a pointer outside the sheet.
verifierNotes:
The code at src/ui/play-page.ts:343-350 matches the finding's description. The toggle handler returns early (keeps focus) when document.activeElement is a non-body element outside the sheet. Otherwise it focuses the summary button. The finding's claim is about Safari behavior: a click on a cell is said to leave focus on body or the invoker. I could not confirm that here, and the finding itself rates its confidence as low. Three things weaken it.

- The mechanism rests on browser-specific focus behavior I cannot reproduce or verify from the code. On a light dismiss, the popover hide steps restore focus to the previously focused element only if focus was inside the popover, so the outcome depends on the engine.
- The spec explicitly allows the focus-to-summary behavior when no element is focused. The finding concedes this: it "follows the spec".
- The suggested fix is documentation or an optional tweak, not a defect in the code. The "focus-steal" in Safari is speculative.

I could not positively confirm a wrong mechanism, so by the default rule I refute it.

The guard at src/ui/play-page.ts lines 340-348 is real. The toggle handler returns early only when `document.activeElement` is a non-body element outside the sheet. Otherwise it focuses the summary button. The finding rests on Safari behaviour that I cannot confirm from the code or here: that a click on a cell leaves focus on body or inside the sheet. It also depends on how WebKit restores focus when a popover hides, and on whether a cell is a focusable button. The finding itself rates confidence low, says the behaviour is allowed by the spec, and calls the effect only a possible surprise. No concrete input or state shows a real user losing something. The summary button is a sensible place for focus when no element is focused, and the code path does what the spec says. I could not positively confirm the mechanism, so I refute it by default.
